intro_md:
**Week 1 · Lesson 4 – First day at work (~45 min). Almost all input – very few answers.** 🎧📖

Today you **listen and read a lot** – the same story, many times, with the words in front of you. Only **2 tiny checks** at the end – and a **💬 Ask me** box after each part if you want to ask me something.

| Part | What | Time |
|---|---|---|
| ① Learn | 9 work chunks + *what to do when you miss a word* | 5 min |
| ② Listen & read | Meeting the team – 4 rounds, with notes for every line | 15 min |
| ③ Listen & read | Hope Street Ep. 3 – the whole story as audio + text | 20 min |
| ✓ | 2 quick self-checks + how it felt | 3 min |

💡 **No pressure:** there is nothing to write until the end. Just keep your eyes and ears on the English.

parts.title: Work chunks + what to do when you miss a word
parts.md:
At work, English speakers use **short fixed phrases** – chunks. You don't need to build them word by word. Learn each one as **one block**, like one long word.

| Chunk | What it means | When you hear it |
|---|---|---|
| **How's it going?** | How are you? (friendly) | Answer: *Good, thanks* / **So far so good** |
| **So far so good** | until now, everything is OK | after starting something new |
| **show sb around** | walk with someone and show them a place | *I'll show you around the office.* |
| **let me know** | tell me | *If you need anything, just let me know.* |
| **get the hang of sth** | learn how to do it, slowly | *It takes a while to get the hang of it.* 🇻🇳 *quen tay, nắm được cách* |
| **it takes (a while / 20 minutes) to + V** | the time you need | *It took me twenty minutes to log in.* |
| **I'd love (a coffee)** | I would really like | polite and warm |
| **by the way** | a new small topic | *Where's the kitchen, by the way?* |
| **give sb a hand (with sth)** | help someone | *Could you give me a hand with this box?* |

### When you miss a word – keep going! 🏃
On Day 2 you said: *"If I miss one word, I lose everything after it."* That happens to everyone. Try this today:

1. **Don't stop in your head.** The speaker doesn't stop – you don't stop either.
2. **Hold the gap, catch the next sentence.** The next sentence often explains the word you missed.
3. **Main idea first, details later.** On round 1 you only need *who, where, what's happening*.
4. **The transcript is your friend, not cheating.** Listening while reading teaches your ears what the words *sound* like.

👂 **Press play** – each chunk inside a sentence, at normal speed. The words are already open: **listen and read at the same time**, twice.

listen.text: How's it going so far?
So far so good, thanks.
Could you show Nam around after lunch?
If you need anything, just let me know.
It takes a while to get the hang of everything here.
I'd love another coffee. Where's the kitchen, by the way?
Could you give me a hand with this box? It's heavier than it looks.

parts.title: Meeting the team
parts.md:
![Claire introduces Nam to the team](data/img/w1/l4-cover.webp)

Claire introduces Nam to the team. **Tom talks quickly** – perfect practice.

**4 rounds, normal speed, no answers:**
1. 👀👂 **Listen + read together** (the words are open below). Follow with your eyes.
2. 📝 **Read the notes** below the player – one line at a time.
3. 👀👂 **Listen + read again.** It will feel easier.
4. 👂 **Hide the transcript** and listen once more. If you miss a word – keep going.

#### Notes – line by line
| Line | What it means |
|---|---|
| *He's starting today.* | **He's** = he is. Today is his first day. |
| *How's it going **so far**?* | How are you, until now? – friendly small talk |
| *So far so good.* | Everything is OK until now. |
| ***Although** I got a bit wet* | a small surprise or problem: it rained on him (🇻🇳 *mặc dù*) |
| *You'll **get used to** it.* | **You'll** = you will. It will become normal for you. |
| *I've lived here ten years* | **I've** = I have. He came 10 years ago and still lives here. |
| *could you **show Nam around**?* | walk with Nam and show him the office |
| *that kind of thing* | and similar things |
| *just **let me know*** | just tell me |
| *It **takes a while** to **get the hang of** everything* | you need some time to learn how everything works (🇻🇳 *quen tay*) |
| ***by the way*** | a new small question |
| *The coffee machine is terrible, **though**.* | **though** at the end = but / however |
| *Most of us go to the café downstairs **instead**.* | not the machine → the café |

listen.text: So, Nam, this is the team. Everyone, this is Nam. He's starting today.
Hi, Nam! Nice to meet you. How's it going so far?
Hi, nice to meet you too. So far so good, thanks. Although I got a bit wet on the way here.
Ha! Welcome to Manchester. You'll get used to it. I've lived here ten years and I still forget my umbrella.
Tom, could you show Nam around after lunch? The kitchen, the printer, that kind of thing.
Sure, no problem. And Nam, if you need anything, just let me know. It takes a while to get the hang of everything here.
Thanks, that's really kind. Where's the kitchen, by the way? I'd love another coffee.
Come on, I'll show you now. The coffee machine is terrible, though. Most of us go to the café downstairs instead.

questions.q: 💬 **Ask me** (optional): any line or word that is still unclear? Vietnamese is OK.
questions.placeholder: e.g. What does 'that kind of thing' mean?

parts.title: Hope Street – Episode 3: Names and a Heavy Box
parts.md:
![Nam helps Mr Patel with a heavy box](data/img/w1/l4-patel.webp)

The whole episode is now **audio + text**. Same story, many times – this is how words become automatic.

1. 👀👂 **Listen + read** the whole episode once. Don't stop.
2. 📖 **Read alone**, a bit faster. Use the notes only if you need them.
3. 👀👂 **Listen + read again.**
4. 👂 **(Optional)** Hide the text and just listen – like a podcast.

#### Notes
| Phrase | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *a small Italian place **round the corner*** | a small Italian restaurant very near |
| ***Rather than** asking him to repeat* | **instead of** asking… |
| *It seemed to work.* | It looked OK / it was a good idea. |
| *Give it a month.* | Wait one month (and it will be OK). |
| ***log in*** | enter your name + password on a computer |
| *Claire **stopped by** his desk* | came to his desk for a short time |
| ***In other words**, go home and rest!* | the same idea, said more simply |
| *Margaret has told me all about you.* | (Margaret talks about everyone! 😄) |
| *Of course she has.* | = of course she has told you – Nam is joking |
| *heavier than it looks* | it looks light, but it's heavy |
| ***Even though** he was tired* | he was tired, but he still helped (🇻🇳 *mặc dù*) |

listen.text: At one o'clock, Tom took Nam to lunch at a small Italian place round the corner. Tom talked fast. Very fast. And Nam understood about half of it. Rather than asking him to repeat everything, Nam smiled and nodded. It seemed to work.
So how long have you been in Manchester?
Two days. I'm still getting used to the weather.
Everyone says that. Give it a month. You won't even notice the rain.

The afternoon was harder. Nam met eight people, and by four o'clock he had forgotten six of their names. Although everyone was friendly, his head was full. He spent an hour on his new laptop, and it took him twenty minutes just to log in.
At half past five, Claire stopped by his desk.
How was your first day?
Good. Tiring, but good.
That's normal. The first week is always the hardest. In other words, go home and rest!
When Nam got back to Hope Street, a man with a beard and a brown jacket was carrying a big box up the stairs.
Oh, you must be the new neighbour. I'm Raj Patel, Flat 3. Margaret has told me all about you.
Of course she has.
And they both laughed.
Could you give me a hand with this? It's a new TV, and it's heavier than it looks.
Even though he was tired, Nam picked up the other end of the box. Two days in Manchester, and he already knew four people on Hope Street. That felt like a good start.

parts.title: Two tiny checks (answers straight away)
parts.md: Just to see what stayed with you. Tap – you'll see the answer at once.

questions.q: Tom says *"It takes a while to get the hang of everything here."* He means…
options: You need time to learn how things work here.
You must work late every day.

check.answer: You need time to learn how things work here.
check.why: **get the hang of sth** = slowly learn how to do it. **takes a while** = needs some time.

questions.q: Why did Nam help Mr Patel, *even though* he was tired?
options: Mr Patel asked him to give him a hand with a heavy TV.
He wanted to see the new TV.

check.answer: Mr Patel asked him to give him a hand with a heavy TV.
check.why: *"Could you **give me a hand** with this? It's a new TV, and it's heavier than it looks."*

questions.q: How much did you understand on the **first** listen + read? Write a number, e.g. 80
Which helped most: listening with the words, the notes, or listening without the words? (optional, Vietnamese OK)
